properties.claim: Current Ω defines the signed Recipe as the only grantor: manifests request capabilities, while the recipe grants capabilities and routed contracts.
The current µhost verifies manifests, recipe/content hashes, spawns isolated worker compartments, verifies host-side capability tokens, and refuses invalid compositions.
vivim.vault is a current Ω plugin with append, revisioned objects, provenance refs, verify, compaction, recovery, migration, export and import contracts; D-432 adds crash/recovery discipline.
Current Ω law owns consent, forbidden overlays, policy conflict, privacy taint, invocation frames, standing and audit; external mutations are governed through law-side checks rather than host policy.

properties.claim: Ω has an Intent contract with payloadHash, interpretation, explicit lifecycle states and four-state resolution semantics; D-411 requires one canonical writer path and law decisions may cite intentRef + payloadHash.

vivim.run currently contains bounded task execution, health, process brokering, plan inspection/intervention, watches, budgets, context assembly, badges, simulation, trust, analytics, layout, partial evaluation and liveness.
vivim.mind derives a read-only WorldModel and control portrait from live law registry plus bounded vault reads; it holds no write capability and fails closed on malformed evidence.
Legacy VIVIM models provider interaction as typed capabilities, resolves language to a capability, routes it to a provider and executes through a single capability surface.
Legacy has a concrete ProviderAccount model tying provider identity, email/login state, Chrome profile/debug metadata and provider sessions; it is unique per provider+email.
Legacy separates VIVIM session, ProviderSession and ProfileSession, with provider/account relationships and Chrome profile/slave metadata.
Legacy Conversation and ConversationMessage support live, imported and history-synced conversations, provider/account links, ordering, parentage, provider message ids and identity hashes.
Legacy places ChromeGovernor at the center of CDP/process lifecycle and states a hard Governor Canon: no other engine touches browser/CDP directly.
Legacy contains semantic grounding, selector healing, browser discovery/watchdog, provider discovery and streaming alignment machinery intended to survive changing provider UIs.

Destination evidence explicitly cites legacy CanvasEngine, LivingCanvas, UnifiedEntry, SessionStateProvider, workspaces/presets/adaptive behavior and project/conversation organization as high-value behavioral harvest.

properties.claim: The destination registry defines VS0–VS8 around intent→world/context→capability→routing/authority→work→evidence→user result; these slices are the primary integration test of the reconstructed system.

A Provider identifies an external service class while Account identifies a user's relationship within that provider; Legacy has the concrete relationship but Ω destination still needs a first-class account model.

Legacy separates ProviderSession and ProfileSession; current provider-browser has an explicit live browser session mode. No evidence yet establishes one canonical Ω lifecycle for authentication, expiry, reconnect and account choice.
Current Ω separates routable capability contracts from ProviderRealization records; provider-browser verifies a PROMOTED realization and parser pin before message.send execution.
Canonical intent persistence, capability resolution and law/consent are separate seams; a root request is not equivalent to permission or execution.
Current run/work mechanisms and vault revisions can persist execution evidence, but the product needs a single work lifecycle linking request, progress, waiting, outcome and durable history.
Destination world/canvas reconciliation makes surface a projection of canonical world/evidence; current mind is a bounded derived lens rather than the authoritative world.
Product Instance characterization requires a durable boundary distinct from replaceable binaries and temporary runtime state; current Ω vault is strong but the product wrapper is not assembled.

Destination provider reconciliation separates available realizations from user routing policy; Legacy has preference/routing behavior, but current Ω evidence does not prove a complete durable policy object.

Current Ω has strong implemented and tested substrate layers, but destination documents separately classify product maturity, human usability and sovereignty; code existence must not be promoted into product completeness.

properties.claim: Legacy has concrete ProviderAccount and routing behavior, while destination reconciliation names a missing canonical Ω Account/routing bridge; no current evidence proves a complete destination-grade policy object.

Ω mind is a bounded evidence-derived lens, while destination world reconciliation expects a broader cross-domain world experience; breadth and identity-join rules are not yet proven as one product system.
Product Instance characterization identifies native product lifecycle, durable environment, installation/replacement, recovery and coherent surface as work not supplied by Ω runtime alone.

Browser-mediated external reality is developed, but a general destination model for desktop input, filesystem, native applications, notifications and local-network resources is not yet characterized as one governed substrate.

Destination requires a coherent return-to-user loop for unfinished work, attention, standing intent and recent changes; current Ω run/director/liveness primitives do not establish a product-grade attention model.

Legacy VIVIM makes ChromeGovernor the sole browser/CDP authority, while current Ω provider-browser uses a plugin-local localhost CDP adapter; this is a deliberate architectural divergence between lineages.
